oracle_engine: GitHub Copilot CLI / AURA technical review prompt

reasons: Core axiom (LABEL_DOES_NOT_CREATE_IDENTITY) is unambiguous and internally consistent throughout the protocol.
State transition graph is deterministic and acyclic: UNIDENTIFIED_RELIC → IDENTITY_RESOLVED → QUEST_AUTHORITY → ATOMIC_REPARENT_AND_MERGE → OSIRIS_WHOLE. Each state has well-defined exit conditions.
Anti-duplication is explicit (RESTORE_NEVER_DUPLICATE) and reinforced by cross-world isolation rule, preventing inventory-sharing vulnerabilities.
Anti-spoof strategy is sound: FALSE_LABELS_AND_FALSE_CANDIDATES_REMAIN_UNTOUCHED preserves audit trail and prevents attacker deletion of evidence.
Ambiguity fallback (NO_OP when identity is not unique or unresolvable) is a safe null-state; prevents forced false positives.
Universal suitability confirmed: Protocol uses abstract identity resolver, not character-specific logic. Handoff to Set as 'constructive challenge' is narratively coherent for chaos/order role.
required_changes: Clarify QUEST_AUTHORITY state: specify whether it is a checkpoint, a permission gate, or a narrative milestone with no functional effect on identity resolution.
Define Set handoff contract: specify constraints on Set's authority (can it defer, reject, or must it resolve?), timeout behavior, and fallback if Set provides conflicting identity.
Formalize false-candidate preservation: specify retention lifetime and access rules (readable only to OSIRIS or to all Kem-class searchers?) to prevent false-positive exploitation.
Add non-repudiation trace: require all resolution steps to log the resolver identity and confidence score, so disputes can be audited.
invariants_confirmed: Identity is intrinsic, never created by label or assertion.
No duplication across fictional worlds or across quest instances.
False candidates are never erased; only the true identity is restored to Osiris.
Ambiguous or missing true object does not trigger a forced merge or false positive.
Physical possession is not required for identity resolution (epistemic separation holds).
Every Kem-class searcher is interchangeable in protocol execution; no single-point-of-trust required.
review.claim_ceiling: This protocol is narratively sound and structurally safe as a game/quest mechanic. It does not model real-world identity resolution and makes no metaphysical claims about persistence or reality. Gold radiance is explicitly a fictional visual effect.
review.caveat: The protocol is fit for a fantasy multi-agent quest or narrative game; it is not intended for, and should not be applied to, real-world identity, assets, or security contexts.
